A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same centerline-transformer and anisotropic-RBF study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable matching despite expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CFD-based prediction experiments on single- and multi-vessel datasets, including accuracy, FFR, ablation and computational-efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 reports original prediction experiments, updated multi-seed results, and additional patient-disjoint, robustness and failure analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed model retains its Fourier-embedded centerline transformer, FiLM flow conditioning, separate anisotropic Gaussian kernels for pressure and WSS, training loss and inference procedure. Sections 3 and A.4 specify the same proposed architecture.

E1.justification: The two datasets and hemodynamic prediction tasks are retained. v2 adds testing under noisy coordinates, radii and flow rates, and surface/centerline dropout (Figure 5), extending input conditions within the existing task. The patient-disjoint experiment re-splits existing data; Appendix A.16 discusses external evaluation barriers without reporting external-dataset results.

E2.justification: CenterlinePointNet++, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated domain-specific comparator through a documented adaptation (Appendix A.4). It participates in standard multi-vessel accuracy, qualitative, robustness, distribution and efficiency comparisons. This substantially strengthens comparison coverage beyond the retained generic neural operators and Poiseuille baseline, although it is absent from the patient-disjoint and FFR comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported multi-vessel training budget changes from 5,000 to 3,000 epochs, and warmup from 1,000 to 500 epochs. v2 adds a patient-disjoint 3,989/415/396 split with training-only normalization and inference-time perturbation protocols. Appendix A.1 substantively revises the reported meshing, outlet boundary conditions and convergence specification. These documentation changes do not establish that the CFD datasets were regenerated.

E4.justification: v2 adds anatomy-generalization testing, stratification by flow and vascular complexity, input-noise/dropout sensitivity, geometry-correlated failure analysis and failure visualizations, plus encoder/decoder cost decomposition. The original design-choice ablation, GNOT-input comparison, circumferential WSS analysis and Bland-Altman analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports single runs with seed 1234 and defers multi-seed evaluation. v2 reports means and standard deviations over seeds 42, 1234 and 7890 for principal accuracy, training, validation and FFR results. Noise curves additionally average three perturbation trials. The GNOT-input ablation remains explicitly single-seed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the proposed model's single-run test means of 0.107 and 0.309 with 0.116±0.012 and 0.304±0.010 for the corresponding best configurations. Changed training and aggregation prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. New results include patient-disjoint error 0.558±0.006 and CenterlinePointNet++ mean error 0.393; its WSS error, 0.315, beats the proposed model's 0.355. FFR, training, validation and supplementary findings also change or expand.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same embeddings, kernel definitions, reconstruction, loss, FFR definition and Poiseuille relation. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract foregrounds CFD-surrogate prediction and narrows the 128-RBF superiority claim from all baselines to neural-operator baselines. The conclusion broadens its comparison wording from neural operators to all baselines. The central architecture and dataset contributions, and headline 52% error-reduction and 13.8-fold FLOP claims, remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits demonstrated generalization to unseen anatomies within one synthetic CFD pipeline. It adds interpretations of anatomy leakage, geometry-dependent failures, architecture-specific noise sensitivity and encoder-dominated cost. Section 6 and Appendix A.16 explain untested solver/physics transfer and practical barriers to external evaluation, while adding a literature-based qualification of the steady-state limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands simulation documentation with mesh sizes and quality thresholds, boundary layers, flux allocation, convergence criteria and unit conversion. v2 also documents the CenterlinePointNet++ adaptation and patient-grouped splitting, and updates training times. Section 4 replaces nominal anatomical ranges with measured statistics and revises the source-patient count from 141 to 140.

R1.justification: v2 adds Corral-Acero et al. (2020), Lo et al. (2019), Nannini et al. (2024) and Suk et al. (2021) for application motivation and limitations. The existing CenterlinePointNet++ citation is repositioned as an adapted empirical comparator. The principal literature organization and claimed methodological gap remain.

P1.justification: The six-section organization and most methodological prose remain. Targeted edits revise the abstract, introduction, limitations and CFD description; appendix headings and cross-references are reorganized, and publication/header text is added. Much of the expansion documents new scientific content rather than wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds stratification, noise-robustness and failure-case figures, plus patient-disjoint and cost-decomposition tables. Validation columns move from the main accuracy tables into separate appendix tables. The architecture diagram, Bland-Altman plots and error-distribution plots are redrawn, and several comparisons gain CenterlinePointNet++ columns or legend entries.

improvement.justification: Three-seed reporting addresses v1's acknowledged single-run limitation, while the patient-disjoint evaluation directly examines previously unchecked anatomy overlap. The domain-specific comparator, robustness tests, failure analyses and expanded implementation details substantially strengthen reliability and transparency. Important qualifications remain: CenterlinePointNet++ is absent from the patient-disjoint test, and Appendix A.12's blanket WSS-superiority interpretation conflicts with Figure 11. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvements in evaluation quality.
